annotation.title_clean: Civil Aviation Directive – 6011 Part (II): Unmanned Aircraft System – Agricultural UAS Operations
annotation.title_en: Civil Aviation Directive – 6011 Part (II): Unmanned Aircraft System – Agricultural UAS Operations
annotation.summary_en: Binding directive issued by the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia under the Civil Aviation Act 1969, in force from 15 November 2022. It sets the rules for agricultural drone operations (spraying and surveillance). Operators need an Aerial Work Certificate and must meet requirements on airworthiness, registration, safety management, insurance and remote pilot competency. Autonomous operations are prohibited.
key_provisions_or_claims: Agricultural UAS operations require a valid Aerial Work Certificate (private or commercial) issued by the CAAM, with a five-phase certification process.
Autonomous operations (where the remote pilot cannot intervene) are not allowed; flights must stay within VLOS/EVLOS, below 400 ft AGL and at least 50 m from uninvolved persons.
Operators must hold third-party liability insurance and run a safety management system with an Accountable Manager, a Safety Manager and other nominated post holders.
Drones must meet airworthiness requirements, carry CAAM registration markings and be maintained by authorised technical personnel; records must be kept for 3 years.
Only pesticides and agricultural payloads approved by the Department of Agriculture may be dispensed; occurrence reporting and audits are required.
